questions.q: In Compose, how does the api service reach the db service?
options: Only by the db container's randomly assigned IP address
By the hostname db -- Compose puts every service in the file on one shared network and resolves service names automatically
It can't; separate services in a compose.yaml can never talk to each other
Only through a volume mounted into both containers
questions.explain: Compose's default network gives each service a DNS entry matching its service name, so api can simply connect to the hostname db.

questions.q: What does depends_on: [db] on the api service actually guarantee?
options: That db is fully initialized and ready to accept connections before api starts
Only that Compose starts the db container before starting the api container -- not that db has finished starting up
That api and db share the same filesystem
That db will restart automatically if api crashes
questions.explain: depends_on controls start order only. Whether the dependency is actually ready is a separate problem -- the one Lesson 25's health checks address.

questions.q: Why does Northbridge's db service use a named volume (db-data) instead of no volume at all?
options: Postgres requires at least one exposed port to function
Without a volume, all of the database's data would be lost the moment the container is removed
Named volumes make Postgres queries run faster
Compose refuses to start a database image without a declared volume
questions.explain: A container's own writable layer disappears when the container is removed. A named volume keeps db-data's actual files on disk, outliving the container.

questions.q: In the example compose.yaml, what is the practical effect of api's environment: DB_HOST: db?
options: It renames the db container to literally 'DB_HOST'
It tells the application code which hostname to connect to for the database -- the Compose service name, db
It sets Postgres's root password
It has no real effect and is purely cosmetic
questions.explain: DB_HOST is just an environment variable the api application reads to know which host to connect to -- here, the Compose service name db, resolved via the default network.

questions.q: How many networks does Compose create by default for a compose.yaml with three services and no explicit networks: configuration?
options: Three, one per service
Zero -- containers must be connected manually
One default network shared by every service in the file
It depends on how many ports: entries are declared
questions.explain: Unless you define custom networks, Compose creates a single default network and attaches every service in the file to it.
